explanation.title: Spanish Passive & Impersonal Constructions: Expressing Actions Without Specific Actors

sections.subtitle: Passive Voice with SER: True Passive
sections.content:
🔄 TRUE PASSIVE VOICE

Uses SER + PAST PARTICIPLE
Emphasizes action or receiver (not doer)

📋 FORMATION:
SER (conjugated) + past participle (agrees!) + POR (by) + agent (optional)

💡 Compare Active vs Passive:

ACTIVE:
→ Cervantes escribió el libro
(Cervantes wrote the book - focus on Cervantes)

PASSIVE:
→ El libro fue escrito por Cervantes
(Book was written by Cervantes - focus on book)

⚠️ PARTICIPLE MUST AGREE with subject:

→ La carta fue escrita por María
(Letter was written - escrita fem sing agrees with carta)

→ Los documentos fueron firmados por el director
(Documents were signed - firmados masc plural agrees with documentos)

→ Las casas fueron construidas en 1950
(Houses were built - construidas fem plural agrees with casas)

📍 AGENT (optional):

Introduced by POR (by):
→ El edificio fue diseñado por un arquitecto famoso
(Building was designed by a famous architect)

Often agent is omitted when unknown/unimportant:
→ El ladrón fue arrestado
(Thief was arrested - by whom not specified)

💡 NOTE:
Spanish passive with SER less common than English
Mainly used in formal written Spanish (journalism, academic writing)

sections.subtitle: Passive SE: The Reflexive Passive
sections.content:
🔄 PASSIVE SE (much more common!)

SE + verb = passive meaning
Very natural in everyday Spanish

📋 FORMATION:
SE + third person verb (agrees with grammatical subject)

Used when agent not mentioned or is general/unknown

💡 Examples:

→ Se habla español aquí
(Spanish is spoken here)
→ Literally: Spanish speaks itself here

→ Se venden casas
(Houses are sold / Houses for sale)
→ Plural venden agrees with casas plural

→ Se firmó el contrato
(Contract was signed)
→ Singular firmó agrees with contrato singular

→ Se escribieron las cartas
(Letters were written)
→ Plural escribieron agrees with cartas plural

⚖️ AGREEMENT RULE:

Verb MUST agree in number with grammatical subject

→ Se construyó una casa
(singular subject → singular verb)

→ Se construyeron dos casas
(plural subject → plural verb)

📋 Grammatical subject usually comes AFTER verb

📍 Common in signs:
→ Se alquila apartamento (Apartment for rent)
→ Se buscan empleados (Employees wanted)
→ Se prohíbe fumar (Smoking prohibited)

💡 Passive SE emphasizes action/result (not who does it)
Much more natural than SER passive in spoken Spanish!

sections.subtitle: ESTAR + Participle: Resultant State
sections.content:
📍 ESTAR + PAST PARTICIPLE

Describes a STATE or CONDITION
Result of previous action (not the action itself)

✅ Focus on CURRENT STATE:

→ La puerta está cerrada
(Door is closed - current state)
→ Someone closed it before

💡 Compare with passive:
→ La puerta fue cerrada por Juan
(Door was closed by Juan - action/process)

vs

→ La puerta está cerrada
(Door is closed - current state)

📋 More examples:

→ Los documentos están firmados
(Documents are signed - they're in a signed state now)

→ La carta está escrita
(Letter is written - completed, current state)

→ Las ventanas están abiertas
(Windows are open - current state)

⚖️ Participle AGREES like an adjective

🎯 Key distinction:

ESTAR = state/condition
SER = action/process

💡 Compare:

→ La casa fue construida en 1950
(House was built in 1950 - action, when it happened, SER for process)

vs

→ La casa está construida
(House is built - current state, completed, ESTAR for result)

📋 Common states:
• estar roto/a (broken)
• estar cerrado/a (closed)
• estar abierto/a (open)
• estar escrito/a (written)
• estar hecho/a (done/made)
• estar muerto/a (dead)
• estar lleno/a (full)
• estar vacío/a (empty)

💡 Focus: ESTAR describes how things ARE NOW as result of past actions

sections.subtitle: Impersonal Expressions: ES + Adjective/Noun + QUE
sections.content:
💭 IMPERSONAL EXPRESSIONS WITH ES

Express general opinions, necessity, judgments
No specific person thinks/feels this way

📋 PATTERN:
ES + adjective/noun + QUE + subjunctive (usually)

📍 Common adjectives:

• ES IMPORTANTE QUE (it's important that)
→ Es importante que estudies

• ES NECESARIO QUE (it's necessary that)
→ Es necesario que vengas

• ES POSIBLE QUE (it's possible that)
→ Es posible que llueva

• ES PROBABLE QUE (it's probable that)
→ Es probable que lleguen tarde

• ES IMPOSIBLE QUE (it's impossible that)
→ Es imposible que sea verdad

• ES MEJOR QUE (it's better that)
→ Es mejor que esperemos

• ES BUENO/MALO QUE (it's good/bad that)
→ Es bueno que practiques

• ES RARO/EXTRAÑO QUE (it's strange that)
→ Es raro que no haya llamado

• ES URGENTE QUE (it's urgent that)
→ Es urgente que respondas

✅ With certainty expressions → INDICATIVE:

→ Es verdad que estudia
(It's true he studies - indicative, it's a fact)

→ Es cierto que viene
(It's certain he's coming - indicative)

→ Es obvio que sabe
(It's obvious he knows - indicative)

📋 PATTERN:
Doubt/opinion/value judgment → subjunctive
Certainty/fact → indicative

💡 Noun forms:
→ Es una pena que (it's a pity that)
→ Es una lástima que (it's a shame that)
Also take subjunctive

sections.subtitle: Impersonal SE: Expressing General 'They/One/People'
sections.content:
👥 IMPERSONAL SE

Expresses actions without specifying WHO does them
Equivalent to: one/you/people/they (general statements)

📋 FORMATION:
SE + third person SINGULAR verb (always singular!)

Used for general statements about what people do

💡 Examples:

→ Se come bien en España
(One eats well in Spain / People eat well / You eat well)
→ General statement

→ Se vive tranquilo aquí
(One lives peacefully here / People live peacefully)

→ Se trabaja mucho en esta empresa
(People work a lot in this company)

→ Se duerme mal con ruido
(One sleeps badly with noise)

⚠️ KEY DIFFERENCE from passive SE:

IMPERSONAL SE doesn't have grammatical subject
(thing being acted upon)
It's about people in general doing something

→ Se estudia mucho
(People study a lot - no object, IMPERSONAL)
Always singular verb

vs

→ Se estudian idiomas
(Languages are studied - plural verb agrees with idiomas, PASSIVE SE)

📋 Summary:
IMPERSONAL = always singular verb, no specific subject
PASSIVE = verb agrees with grammatical subject

💡 Other uses:

→ Se dice que... (It is said that... / They say that...)
→ Se cree que... (It is believed that...)
→ Se piensa que... (It is thought that...)
→ Se sabe que... (It is known that...)

Very common for expressing general wisdom or common knowledge!

sections.subtitle: Third Person Plural for Impersonal: General 'They'
sections.content:
👥 THIRD PERSON PLURAL (impersonal)

Can express impersonal meaning
Equivalent to English 'they' when referring to:
• People in general
• Authorities
• Unspecified groups

📋 Simply use third person plural verb (ellos/ellas form)
Without stating the subject

💡 Examples:

→ Dicen que va a llover
(They say it's going to rain)
→ People in general say

→ Construyeron un edificio nuevo
(They built a new building)
→ Someone/authorities built, unspecified

→ Llamaron a la puerta
(They knocked / Someone knocked)
→ Unspecified person

→ Robaron el banco
(They robbed the bank)
→ Unknown robbers

→ Abrieron una tienda nueva
(They opened a new store)
→ Unspecified who

💡 Very natural when you don't know or don't want to specify WHO

🔄 THREE WAYS to express similar ideas:

1️⃣ IMPERSONAL SE:
→ Se habla español
(Spanish is spoken - focus on language)

2️⃣ PASSIVE SE:
→ Se construyeron casas
(Houses were built - focus on houses)

3️⃣ THIRD PERSON PLURAL:
→ Construyeron casas
(They built houses - focus on unspecified people building)

💬 Especially common in spoken Spanish and narratives
When actor is unknown or unimportant

→ Me dijeron que cerrarían temprano
(They told me they would close early)

→ Vendieron todo
(They sold everything)

questions.question: How do you form the true passive voice in Spanish?
questions.hint: True passive: SER + past participle. Example: fue escrito (was written).

questions.question: 'El libro fue escrito por Cervantes' - Does 'escrito' agree?

answers.text: No - past participles with ser never change

questions.hint: With SER passive, participle agrees with subject. Libro (masculine singular) → escrito.

questions.question: 'Las casas fueron construid___' - Complete the participle.

answers.text: construidas (feminine plural to agree with casas)

questions.hint: SER passive: participle agrees with subject. Casas (feminine plural) → construidas.

questions.question: What introduces the agent in passive voice?
questions.hint: Agent introduced by POR: fue escrito POR Cervantes (was written BY Cervantes).

questions.question: 'Se habla español aquí' - What does this mean?
questions.hint: SE + verb = passive construction. Se habla español = Spanish is spoken.

questions.question: 'Se vende casa' vs 'Se venden casas' - Why different verbs?

answers.text: Verb agrees with subject: casa (singular) vs casas (plural)

questions.hint: Passive se: verb agrees with grammatical subject. Casa (singular) → vende. Casas (plural) → venden.

questions.question: 'Se construyó una casa' vs 'Se construyeron dos casas' - Why?

answers.text: Singular subject (una casa) vs plural subject (dos casas)
Una requires singular, dos requires plural
No difference, both are correct for both

questions.hint: Passive se verb agrees with subject. Una casa (one house - singular) → construyó. Dos casas (plural) → construyeron.

questions.question: Which is more common in spoken Spanish for passive meaning?
questions.hint: Passive SE is much more common in spoken Spanish than ser passive (which is formal/written).

questions.question: 'La puerta está cerrada' - What does this express?

answers.text: Current state/condition (the door is closed - resultant state)
Action of closing (someone is closing the door)
Future action (the door will be closed)

questions.hint: ESTAR + participle = resultant state/condition. The door IS closed (current state).

questions.question: 'La casa fue construida' vs 'La casa está construida' - What's the difference?

answers.text: FUE = action/process (was built); ESTÁ = current state (is built/finished)
No difference, both mean exactly the same
FUE is past, ESTÁ is present
FUE is formal, ESTÁ is informal

questions.hint: SER (fue) = action/process of building. ESTAR (está) = current state of being built/finished.

questions.question: 'Los documentos están firmados' - Does 'firmados' agree?

answers.text: No - with estar, participle never changes

questions.hint: With ESTAR, participle agrees like adjective. Documentos (masculine plural) → firmados.

questions.question: 'Es importante que estudies' - Why subjunctive 'estudies'?

answers.text: Impersonal expressions of opinion/value require subjunctive

questions.hint: ES + adjective (opinion/value) + QUE → subjunctive. Es importante que estudies.

questions.question: 'Es necesario que vengas' - Why subjunctive 'vengas'?
questions.hint: ES NECESARIO QUE (it's necessary that) requires subjunctive: vengas.

questions.question: 'Es verdad que estudia' - Why indicative 'estudia'?
questions.hint: ES VERDAD (it's true - certainty/fact) → indicative. Es verdad que estudia (indicative).

questions.question: 'Es posible que llueva' vs 'Es cierto que llueve' - Why different moods?

answers.text: Possibility (es posible) → subjunctive; Certainty (es cierto) → indicative

questions.hint: Doubt/possibility → subjunctive (llueva). Certainty/fact → indicative (llueve).

questions.question: 'Se come bien en España' - What does SE express here?
questions.hint: IMPERSONAL SE = one/people in general. Se come = one eats / people eat.

questions.question: 'Se trabaja mucho' vs 'Se trabajan mucho' - Which is correct for impersonal?

answers.text: Se trabaja (impersonal se always uses singular verb)
Depends on number of people working

questions.hint: IMPERSONAL SE always takes SINGULAR verb. Se trabaja mucho (people work a lot).

questions.question: 'Se estudia mucho' vs 'Se estudian idiomas' - What's the difference?

answers.text: First is impersonal (people study); second is passive (languages are studied)
First is singular subject, second is plural

questions.hint: Impersonal (no object) = singular verb. Passive (with object) = verb agrees with object.

questions.question: 'Se dice que...' means...

answers.text: It is said that... / They say that... (impersonal)

questions.hint: Se dice = it is said / they say (impersonal - general wisdom/common knowledge).

questions.question: 'Dicen que va a llover' - Who is 'dicen' referring to?
questions.hint: Third person plural without subject = impersonal 'they/people'. Dicen = they say (general).

questions.question: 'Robaron el banco' (without mentioning who) means...

answers.text: They robbed the bank (someone/unknown people robbed it)

questions.hint: Third person plural without explicit subject = unspecified 'they'. Robaron = they robbed (unknown who).

questions.question: 'Construyeron un edificio nuevo' - Who built it?
questions.hint: Third person plural without subject = impersonal construction. Someone/they built (unspecified).

questions.question: Which expresses 'Spanish is spoken here'?
questions.hint: Passive se: Se habla español (Spanish is spoken - singular verb with singular subject español).

questions.question: Three ways to say 'Houses were built': Which is most formal/written?

answers.text: Las casas fueron construidas (SER passive - formal)

questions.hint: SER + participle (fueron construidas) is most formal, mainly used in writing/journalism.
